name: How do I know if a cabinet finish is truly custom?

mainEntity.name: What makes a finish custom instead of a standard manufacturer color or stock stain?
mainEntity.text: What makes a finish custom instead of a standard manufacturer color or stock stain?

acceptedAnswer.text: A finish is truly custom when it is developed for the specific project rather than selected from a limited stock list. That can mean matching a paint color to existing trim, blending stains to fit a particular wood species, adjusting sheen, adding glaze, or building a multi-step finish that changes the tone and depth. In luxury cabinetry, custom often also includes how the finish performs, not just how it looks. A shop may create spray-outs, sample doors, or mockups to confirm the final effect in the actual room. If a builder claims the finish is custom, ask what part of the process was actually tailored: color, sheen, texture, aging, or protection. The most reliable sign is documented approval of a physical sample before production begins.
acceptedAnswer.description: A custom finish is typically mixed, tested, or adjusted for a specific project rather than pulled from a standard catalog color. It may include custom stain blending, sheen adjustment, glazing, distressing, or color matching to existing architectural elements. The best proof is a sample board approved for the exact project conditions.
